Like numerous related poems in the Apadāna that celebrate gifts of fruit, the text commemorates the past merit of an elder who offered an *āmaṇḍa* fruit to a Buddha, describing the subsequent celestial rewards and eventual attainment of arahantship. SuttaCentral records translations of the text in five languages, but lists no established parallels in non-Pali corpora [SuttaCentral].
